mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the federal funds rate over 3 consecutive months indicates the Federal Reserve is shifting from tightening to easing, which lowers discount rates and increases the present value of future equity cash flows, producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns in easing periods are not significantly higher than baseline (t-test p > 0.05), or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the federal funds rate above 5.25% triggers a risk-off reaction in equity markets, compressing discount rates and reducing the present value of future cash flows, producing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns in rate hike periods are not significantly lower than baseline (t-test p > 0.05), or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in monthly employment growth (PAYEMS) above 200,000 jobs indicates a strengthening labor market, which boosts consumer confidence and corporate earnings expectations, producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns in strong employment periods are not significantly higher than baseline (t-test p > 0.05), or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in monthly employment growth (PAYEMS) below -50,000 jobs indicates a weakening labor market, which raises uncertainty and compresses earnings expectations, producing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns in weak employment periods are not significantly lower than baseline (t-test p > 0.05), or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window.
